newsitem.title: USA: US debt, equity issuance set record in '96 - report.
newsitem.headline: US debt, equity issuance set record in '96 - report.

text.p: Corporate America issued debt and equity securities at a record pace in 1996, taking advantage of low interest rates to refinance debt or raise new capital amid tame inflation and strong investor demand, research firm Securities Data Co reported.
Issuance of debt and equity securities jumped nearly 34 percent in 1996 to more than $953 billion from $712 billion in 1995, Securities Data said.
Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, top underwriter of U.S. debt and equity issues since 1988, kept its spot, underwriting $156 billion in securities in 1996, up from $126.4 billion in 1995.
Lehman Brothers came in second place in 1996, whle Goldman Sachs & Co was the third leading U.S. underwriter, Securities Data said.
A variety of categories set new records in 1996 including equities, initial public offerings, straight corporate debt and asset-backed securities, Securities Data said.
Straight debt issuance totaled $535 billion in 1996 compared with $443 billion in 1995.
Mortgage and asset-backed securities continued their strong advance as more than $247 billion was raised in 1996 compared to less than $156 billion last year.
Equity offerings exceeded an unprecedented $115 billion in 1996 versus $82 billion in the prior year.
Straight preferred stock likewise exhibited spectacular volume, with a record $32 billion coming to market in 1996, eclipsing last year's volume of under $13 billion.

In the fourth quarter of 1996, the number of debt and equity issues exceeded 2,000 for the third consecutive quarter, while for the third straight quarter more than $200 billion was underwritten by Wall Street, the research firm said.
Issuance volume for the fourth quarter hit $251.5 billion, making it the fifth-best quarter ever. In first place is the third quarter of 1993, with volume of $295 billion.
Issuance of domestic corporate investment grade debt rose by over 22 percent from the prior year to over $301.4 billion, research firm Securities Data Co reported.
Public domestic corporate junk bond issuance climbed to 29 billion in 1996 compared to $25.2 billion last year.
Combined public and private (144A) high-yield bond deals approached the record level of $73 billion set in 1993, the company said.
